title: Automated residency & retention policy enforcer with drift-healing playbooks
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Implement an end-to-end policy-as-code enforcement pipeline that ensures data residency and retention configurations remain compliant, detects configuration drift across hosted/dedicated/private deployments, and remediates or escalates with automated evidence/reporting.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Repo of residency & retention policies expressed in Rego (OPA) and a canonical YAML schema for retention windows.
2) Drift detector that compares desired policy state (git) with live configuration for: S3 buckets/object lifecycle, DB region tags, KMS key region bindings, message retention settings.
3) Automated remediation options: a) safe automated heal (idempotent infra change), b) create incident with remediation playbook, c) rollback to last-approved config.
4) Evidence bundle produced for each remediation event containing signed policy version, diff, executed actions, timestamps, and proof-of-delivery path (S3) — accessible from Console.
5) Can be enabled per-customer with opt-in policy and role-based approvals; demo run on staging with synthetic drift cases and zero customer-facing downtime.
6) Unit/integration tests and k8s e2e that validate detector and remediation flows.
7) Metrics exported: drift_count, time_to_remediate, false_positive_rate, evidence_generation_latency.
design_notes:
We will reuse OPA/Rego for policy evaluation to keep expression language consistent with other infra checks. The detector will run as an idempotent controller: snapshot desired state from a policy-config repo (git) and compare with live config via provider adapters (aws, gcp, internal control plane). Remediation actions will be defined as parameterized playbooks (Terraform apply with targeted resources or API calls) and safe-guards include dry-run, approval gates, and rate limits. Evidence bundles will be signed with the platforms KMS key and stored in a tenants/<<tenant-id>>/compliance-evidence/<timestamp>.zip S3 prefix. We'll integrate with Console to show a timeline and link the bundle. For private deployments an agent will run locally and upload signed evidence to customer S3 or provide an on-prem archive path.

Key technical trade-offs considered:
- Strong enforcement vs customer impact: make automatic heals opt-in and default to create incidents.
- Rego vs custom DSL: choose Rego for community support and existing policy libraries.
- Remediation surface: prefer API-driven fixes over direct infra patches where possible to respect ownership boundaries.

Security: all remediation actions must be audited, limited by role, and gated by release toggles. Evidence must be tamper-evident and retained according to retention policies for audits.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): policy schema + Rego library, git-backed canonical policy repo, detector prototype for S3 lifecycle and KMS bindings.
Phase 2 (2 sprints): remediation playbook runner, approvals UI hooks in Console, evidence bundle format and signer.
Phase 3 (1 sprint): integration with Dedicated/Private agents, canary rollout to test customers, metric dashboards and alerting.
Phase 4 (ongoing): expand provider adapters, add DB/stream retention checks, reduce false positives via heuristics.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: false positives cause unnecessary churn. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, dry-run first, manual approval by default.
- Risk: remediation causes outages. Mitigation: rate limits, canary scope (single resource), circuit-breaker to stop automated heals.
- Risk: evidence being large or leaking PII. Mitigation: sanitize evidence, redact secrets, compress & encrypt bundles per-tenant.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for Rego policies and policy schema.
- Integration test harness that injects synthetic drift in staging (e.g., change S3 lifecycle, move resource region tag) and validates detector identifies drift.
- Remediation acceptance tests: automated heal and approval flows.
- e2e with private agent running behind VPC to ensure signed evidence can be placed on customer storage.
- Load test detector at 10k resources to validate scalability and batching.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy detector + Rego policy read-only mode to staging; run for 2 weeks to collect signal.
2) Enable remediation in staging with dry-run on production shadow mode.
3) Soft launch for 3 pilot enterprise customers with explicit opt-in and SSO approval gates.
4) Gradual enablement by customer cohorts; monitor drift metrics and rollback on anomaly.
5) Mark GA after 3 months of stable pilot results.
